faq.q: Does dragging to reorder work on a phone?
faq.a: Yes. Reordering is built on pointer events rather than the HTML5 drag-and-drop API, so the same press-and-drag gesture works with a mouse on desktop and a finger on a touch screen. A marker shows whether the page will drop before or after the card you are hovering over. Every card also has ▲ and ▼ buttons that move it one slot, which work by keyboard and are there for accessibility when dragging is not convenient.

faq.q: If I delete a page by mistake, can I get it back?
faq.a: Yes. Deleting one page, or several selected pages at once, stores them so an "Undo delete" button can restore them to their original positions. The button shows how many pages are waiting to be restored. Undo holds the most recent delete; once you make another delete, that becomes the undoable one. You can also select multiple pages (tap to toggle the highlight) and rotate or delete them together.

faq.q: Can I combine pages from another PDF, add blanks, or duplicate a page?
faq.a: Yes to all three. "Add pages from another PDF" appends every page of a second file to the grid, where you can then drag them anywhere. "Blank page at end" inserts an empty page the size of the first page in the document. The duplicate button on each card drops an identical copy right after it. Password-protected or unreadable second files are skipped with a message rather than breaking the batch.

faq.q: Is the page content kept intact, and what is the saved file called?
faq.a: Yes — pages are copied with pdf-lib's copyPages, which preserves the original content exactly rather than re-rendering it to an image. Any rotation you applied is added on top of the page's existing rotation, so a page already stored rotated stays correct. Blank pages are added at the chosen size. The result downloads as your-file-organized.pdf, and because everything runs in your browser the PDFs are never uploaded.
